newsitem.title: PERU: Peru tries to get jailed rebels to stop siege.
newsitem.headline: Peru tries to get jailed rebels to stop siege.

text.p: Peruvian intelligence officers have met jailed Marxist rebels and tried -- so far fruitlessly -- to persuade them to publicly condemn their comrades's takeover of the Japanese ambassador's residence, police sources said on Friday.

The sources told Reuters a group of National Intelligence Service (SIN) officers had spoken to the jailed leader of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), Victor Polay, at his solitary confinement cell in a military jail.

It was MRTA rebels who travelled from jungle hideouts to storm the residence on Tuesday night, taking prisoner a glittering array of ministers, ambassadors and businessmen to press their demands for the release of Polay and other jailed MRTA members.

The sources also said SIN officers were speaking to other imprisoned MRTA leaders serving life sentences such as Peter Cardenas and Lucero Cumpa to demand they also call for an end to the embassy siege, now in its third day.

The government wanted them to sign a public letter denouncing the attack and repudiating their movement's tactics, just as rival guerrilla leader Abimael Guzman had done with his Maoist Shining Path movement in 1993 after being captured, they added.

Local newspaper La Republica said Canadian ambassador Anthony Vincent, who has been acting as one of the crisis mediators after being released from the residence, would meet Polay at the hostage-takers' request. This could not be officially confirmed.
Fujimori has not made any public statement on the crisis since it began. He was spending Friday closeted with generals and security chiefs at a military barracks in the capital.
